To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IoT apps have a unique structure, they have a large number of interactions with devices and online services, and they have unique idiosyncrasics that make program analysis challenging.

(i) the IoT ecosystem is a complex, heterogeneous, and dynamic system; (ii) IoT apps are written in multiple programming languages, and each programming language has its own idio-syncrasies; (iii) IoT apps have different security and privacy requirements; (iv) there is an increasing number of IoT devices that are connected to the Internet; (v) IoT devices and apps interact with each others, and the interaction between apps, in particular, is not well studied; and
IoT apps are written in multiple programming languages and are often short and simple, but their complexity is increased when they use external libraries and when they use the IoT platform’s APIs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
program analysis for IoT security and privacy.
the security and privacy of commodity IoT devices and applications
the security and privacy of IoT apps, which is a challenging task due to the nature of IoT applications, their idiosyncrasics, and the analysis requirements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the analysis of IoT applications is a challenging problem that requires a multi-faceted solution.
there is no conclusive statement. There are several reasons for the lack of conclusive statements.

the current IoT ecosystem is not ready for security and privacy analysis, and we need to address several fundamental issues.
